
### exit statuses 

```c
int main() {
    return 0;  /* or exit(0); */
}
```


### the status  {.smaller}


```c
#include <sys/wait.h>
...
pid_t pid = waitpid(child_pid, &status, 0);
if (pid == (pid_t) -1) { /* waitpid failed */ }
} else if (WIFEXITED(status)) {
  printf("main returned or exit called with %d\n", WEXITSTATUS(status));
} else if (WIFSIGNALED(status)) {
  printf("killed by signal %d\n", WTERMSIG(status))
  printf("signal description: %s\n", strsignal(WTERMSIG(status)));
} else {
  ... /* not possible? */
}
```

- "status code" encodes _both return value and if exit was abnormal_
- `W*` macros to decode it


### "signals" {.smaller}

*  POSIX mechanism to let processes handle special events
*  example: control-C usually results in SIGINT (interrupt) signal
   *  SIGINT is an integer constant in signal.h
   *  by default: SIGINT terminates process
   *  process can install "handler" to override this behavior
*  some other notable "signals":
   *  SIGHUP (hang up; terminal went away when process still running)
   *  SIGTERM (terminate), SIGKILL (unoverridable terminate)
   *  SIGSEGV (segmentation fault), SIGBUS (bus error), SIGFPE (floating point exception)
